statement: For a typed cascade C with CTMT-stuck verdict blocked at external theorem X, a manager-led paper-grounded audit may resolve X.
When X is inherited, the cascade-internal reduction blocked by X becomes executable.
Executing the reduction typically exposes a deeper typed gate X_next rather than closing the parent residual.
The CTMT classification persists; the stuck-at object refines.
The recursion terminates at precision-limited, theorem-unstated-in-literature, known-barrier, or genuine-closure termini.
The terminal-object form adapts across tracks while preserving the typed-condition shape.

proof_outline: At cascade level n, X_n is a named external theorem, formula, construction, estimate, or atlas condition.
Literature audit can promote X_n from unavailable to inherited content.
The cascade then performs the previously blocked reduction.
The reduction reveals either extra hypotheses in X_n, mismatch between X_n and the framework need, or a finer terminal object.
This creates X_{n+1}; the stuck object changes but the terminal typed condition persists.
Iteration stops only at precision limitation, missing literature, foundational barrier, or closure.
